newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Power rate cut to begin Russian monopoly reform.
newsitem.headline: Power rate cut to begin Russian monopoly reform.

text.p: Russia will begin the huge task of reforming its monopoly firms by cutting tariffs at national power utility Unified Energy System (UES), First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Wednesday.

"We shall start with cutting tariffs at RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES), then we shall deal with transportation tariffs and at the last stage we shall deal with Gazprom efficiency," Nemtsov told a news conference.

Nemtsov, who has been charged by President Boris Yeltsin with untangling the messy bureaucracy and low productivity of Russia's "natural monopolies," said the state would develop concrete measures to pay UES's debts and raise its efficiency.
But he said the government would not make quick steps in reforming monopolies.
"Caution and accuracy here is more important than the speed of making decisions," he said.
Last month Yeltsin slammed Russia's monopoly firms for unjustifiably high prices.

The monopolies are the government's newest makeover target, castigated for functioning largely as they did in Soviet days, when production costs were irrelevant, competition non-existent and prices bore no relationship to reality.

Energy prices for industrial consumers have risen steeply during post-Soviet reform, but household rates have been much less affected and as a result no rates reflect market principles or production costs.
Nemtsov said that the monopolies, including the Railway Ministry, th Gazprom natural gas producer and UES were the biggest debtors to Russia's Pension Fund.
The Railway Ministry's debt amounts to 3.3 trillion roubles and UES debt is over over trillion roubles, Nemtsov said.
Overall debt to the Pension Fund is 60 trillion roubles, while the Pension Fund owes 11 trillion roubles to pensioners, he said.
